Subject: Interim coverage confirmation needed for procurement window

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you're well. We are finalizing our vendor security sign-off for an enterprise rollout and noticed Redwood's last SOC 2 Type II report covers the period through 2026-06-30. Our procurement and legal teams require a short interim/bridge confirmation that the controls in-scope have remained in effect from 2026-07-01 through the current date (or an explanation of any material changes).

Specifically, can you provide:
- A one-page bridge/continuity statement referencing the SOC 2 report period and confirming no material control changes since 2026-07-01, OR a clear list of any control deltas.
- Confirmation on monitoring/alerting windows for IAM and logging (SOC CC6/CC7 scope items).
- Any supporting artifacts you can share (high level) such as retention configuration snapshots or confirmation of KMS rotation policy.

We have an internal deadline to circulate an approved package to execs by 2026-11-03. Can you let me know whether Redwood can provide a draft bridge letter and a signed attestation or if you prefer a DocuSign flow?

I'm attaching our vendor intake checklist for context. Happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Anita Shah
Head of Procurement, PrismLabs
Anita.Shah@prismlabs.com

Hi Anita,

Thanks for the clear note — we can support this. We typically provide a short bridge letter that: 1) references the SOC 2 Type II report end date (2026-06-30), 2) confirms there were no material control changes in-scope since that date, and 3) lists control areas covered by the attestation.

A couple of quick clarifying questions so the letter meets procurement's needs:
- Do you need itemized evidence (e.g., screenshots or exports) attached, or is a signed letter sufficient for your legal team?
- Is it sufficient to confirm high-level practices for KMS rotation and monitoring windows, or do you need specific timestamps/config snapshots?
- For signature: we can provide a PDF signed by our security lead and also run via DocuSign if you prefer an audit trail.

I'm attaching our standard bridge letter draft for your review (short form). If you can highlight any phrasing you'd like changed, we will produce a signed version within 48 business hours once language is agreed.

Next steps I propose: you redline the attached and return by EOD Friday (2026-10-23) so we can finalize. If that timeline is tight I can schedule a 20-minute alignment call.

Regards,

Kimberly Park
Enterprise Security & Compliance Liaison

Kimberly — thanks, that sounds good. A few notes from our legal and security reviewers (copied):

- A signed letter is preferred; DocuSign is acceptable and may be required by legal for final records.
- Our security team asks that the bridge letter explicitly call out (briefly) the following control domains: IAM, System Logging & Monitoring, Change Management, and Vulnerability Management. A single-sentence confirmation per domain is sufficient.
- For IAM/Logging we would like confirmation that logging retention is at least 90 days for audit logs and that KMS key rotation policies are in place (we don't need rotation logs, just confirmation of policy and rotation cadence).
- If there were any material control changes (e.g., vendor switch for logging, significant policy changes) since 2026-07-01, we need a short explanation.

Procurement note: we will accept the signed PDF by DocuSign if you can route to: procurement@prismlabs.com.

I've attached the checklist again and added two sample redline suggestions in the doc comments. We do not expect export-level evidence at this stage; just the signed bridge letter plus the SOC 2 report reference is sufficient for approval.

Anita
